significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish the form-(iii) predictive coupling that a causally defined “working-memory occupancy” is bounded during CoT and that its “low and stable” state predicts distance to completion and permits compression without comparable accuracy loss; this would constrain when additional tokens are useful, rather than merely showing that an internal feature exists. It establishes both a phenomenon—occupancy rises and falls with reasoning progress—and a proposed register-file mechanism in which quantities are “kept live while still needed” and “freed once consumed”; this directly addresses the per-instance compute-allocation problem highlighted by Snell et al., “Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can Be More Effective Than Scaling Model Parameters,” and the budget-forcing results of Muennighoff et al., “s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling.” The claim is reasonably determinate despite leaving the numerical bound unstated: a negative result could reject the bounded-live-set account or show that occupancy decay does not predict completion, thereby ruling out this specific mechanistic basis for adaptive compression rather than merely reporting a failed probe. In the topic-substitution check, generic efficient-reasoning interpretability would not earn this score; the extra weight comes specifically from the asserted occupancy-to-completion relation, so the claim is above the topic-median direction/probe template but not a field-defining quantitative law.

reach.justification: The named handles are the online “working-memory occupancy” signal and the resulting “training-free adaptive compression” controller, which can trigger “early answer emission when occupancy has been low and stable.” This is ex ante rather than post hoc because it forecasts that further reasoning is largely bookkeeping before those tokens are generated, leaving an action window for systems that gate inference cost or latency. After per-model re-extraction, the hypothesis still predicts a qualitative relation—small, stable occupancy should indicate imminent completion and support more compression—rather than supplying only an uninformative search procedure; its stated scope covers CoT reasoning and multiple task classes, although the claim does not specify a quantitative invariant across architectures. The topic-substitution check does not preserve the score: efficient reasoning alone supplies no such deployable early-exit signal, while this particular conclusion could be used by researchers and practitioners who serve or budget reasoning models, satisfying both lead-time and non-researcher-uptake criteria.
